# Always-feasible middle-face tents and their exact profile constraint

This is a planar three-fiber deformation lemma. It gives an additional actual descent test and an exact necessary condition at an attained local minimum. It does not assert existence of such a minimum or of a negative-cost face. The final example shows that the condition does not imply a pointwise lower bound on face incidence.

## 1. Setting and actual middle-only variation

Let A,K,B be planar convex bodies with (A+B)/2 contained in K, at the three integer bases -1,0,1. Let y0 belong to int K, and let v_0,v_1,v_2 span the plane with sole relation sum v_i=0. Write h_i=h_B(v_i), beta_i=2v_i.y0-h_i. Suppose the actual ambient caps with middle threshold v_i.y0 and B support threshold h_i have common raw mass Q. Assume Q is the true global maximum raw mixed depth.

The K cuts are proper. For the lemma below, each A cut is either proper or has its threshold strictly outside A's support interval. Set sigma_i to its normalized section length when proper and to zero when strictly full or empty. Put

    k_i=H_1(K intersect {v_i.x=v_i.y0})/||v_i||>0,
    lambda_i=1/(k_i+2sigma_i),
    pi_i=lambda_i/sum lambda_i,
    M=|A|+|K|+|B|, r=Q/M,
    W_K(x)=sum_i pi_i 1_(v_i.x>=v_i.y0).

No gap is required below Q for either endpoint maximum. The strictly saturated allowance is useful in the exact example; the all-proper case in the signed-shape theorem is included.

Let F be a nondegenerate whole supporting face of K, with outward unit normal n. Choose ANY p in relint F and enlarge only the middle body:

    K_e=conv(K union {p+e n}),  A_e=A, B_e=B.

This variation is always compatible, since K_e contains K. It requires no feasible-room condition involving A or B. Its three lifted fibers still form an actual convex body with exactly the stated integer sections.

In unit tangential coordinates F=[alpha,beta], let p have coordinate t, and let T_t be its unit-height tent. Then the actual added middle area and cap masses satisfy

    |K_e|-|K|=e(beta-alpha)/2+o(e),
    |(K_e minus K) intersect {v_i.x>=v_i.y0}|
       =e integral_F T_t 1_(v_i.x>=v_i.y0) ds+o(e).       (1)

These are the ordinary convex-body face-bulge formulas proved and independently audited in `candidate 6e9992972c414d73` and `unshared historical review/context (not an accepted premise)`. Their proof uses convergence of the two contact points to the face endpoints and bounds the exterior-face correction by o(e). It does not assume a quadratic remainder at curved joins.

## 2. A single actual meeting point controls every source

The old budget functions are C1 near y0. Strictly saturated A cuts are locally constant, and proper cuts have continuous section lengths. Their source gradients are -(k_i+2sigma_i)v_i. The same weighted Jacobian argument as for the fixed-facet menu proves local invertibility in the source and common budget.

The added K-cap functions have size O(e) and Lipschitz constants tending to zero in the source: a transverse cutting line meets the thin added band in length O(e), while a parallel proper cut has a fixed gap from that band. Applying the local inverse map to the negative added-cap vector is therefore a contraction on a sufficiently large O(e) ball. Its fixed point is an actual y_e=y0+O(e) in int K_e and yields one common budget

    q_e=Q+e integral_F T_t W_K ds+o(e).                 (2)

The middle halfspaces through that point cover the whole plane, since their normals sum to zero. They consequently bound the true depth of every point of the new middle fiber, including new points.

Pointwise, at least one of these three middle halfspaces contains every point, so W_K>=min_i pi_i>0. Hence the coefficient in (2) is strictly positive. Both unchanged endpoint maxima are at most Q and are strictly below q_e for all small positive e, even if both were tied originally. Thus the new GLOBAL maximum is at most q_e.

It follows that

    q_e/[M+|K_e|-|K|]-Q/M
       =(e/M) C_K(t)+o(e),
    C_K(t)=integral_F T_t(s)[W_K(s)-r] ds.              (3)

Therefore C_K(t)<0 gives actual strict normalized-depth descent without endpoint-gap or feasible-room assumptions. At any attained local minimum under these compatible variations, one necessarily has

    C_K(t)>=0 for EVERY supporting segment F
                         and EVERY t in (alpha,beta).   (4)

This is a separate descent option: it does not assert that (4) fails in every below-target configuration.

## 3. Exact Green-potential form and the signed-roof interface

Put f(s)=W_K(s)-r on one face and define

    G_F(t,s)=[min(t,s)-alpha][beta-max(t,s)]/(beta-alpha),
    U(t)=integral_alpha^beta G_F(t,s) f(s) ds.

The function f is bounded and piecewise constant, with only finitely many original cut crossings. Direct differentiation of the two integrals gives U(alpha)=U(beta)=0 and -U''=f almost everywhere; U is C1. The exact tent identity is

    C_K(t)=(beta-alpha)U(t)/[(t-alpha)(beta-t)].        (5)

Consequently the necessary condition (4) is exactly U>=0 on the whole face. In particular U'(alpha)>=0 and U'(beta)<=0. Positive combinations of middle-face tents have nonnegative cost under this condition. The ordinary positive trapezoid in the coupled-face source is such a combination, so its middle cost is nonnegative at a local minimum.

For the signed roof of `candidate b85e6bd6eff40d13`, write the full face as [alpha,beta], the inner base as [alpha0,beta0], and its plateau as [c,d]. Let ell_L=alpha0-alpha and ell_R=beta-beta0. Its signed unit profile is

    H(s)=min{1,(s-alpha0)/(c-alpha0),(beta0-s)/(beta0-d)}.

Integrating -H U'' by parts on its affine pieces, with U=0 at the full-face endpoints, gives the exact identity

    integral_F H(s) f(s) ds
       =[U(c)-ell_L U'(alpha)]/(c-alpha0)
          +[U(d)+ell_R U'(beta)]/(beta0-d).           (6)

The same formula holds when c=d: the two downward slope jumps add. To verify it, the endpoint values of H are -ell_L/(c-alpha0) and -ell_R/(beta0-d), and its second derivative consists of negative point masses of sizes 1/(c-alpha0) and 1/(beta0-d). This proves (6) directly, with every endpoint sign retained.

The signed middle-cost term is one half of (6). Under U>=0 the interior terms are nonnegative and the two outer-trimming terms are nonpositive. Their competition is exact; condition (4) alone does not settle its sign. Thus this interface retains the actual whole-face profile rather than declaring outer intervals favorable from a pointwise inference.

## 4. An actual critical configuration with low face loads but positive tent costs

Let

    T={x<=1, y<=1, -x-y<=1}, |T|=9/2,
    A=(3/5)T, K=-T, B=(4/5)(-T).

Use the canonical normals v_1=(1,0), v_2=(0,1), v_3=(-1,-1) and y0=0. These are actual compatible fibers. Indeed K is described by -v_i.x<=1, while

    h_A(-v_i)=6/5, h_B(-v_i)=4/5,

so every point of (A+B)/2 satisfies every defining inequality of K. Moreover -A is contained in B. Their areas are

    |A|=81/50, |B|=72/25, |K|=9/2, M=9.

For every ambient through-source halfspace, the reflection map (-1,x) to (1,-x) pairs the whole A fiber with a subset of B. Each reflected pair has at least one point in the closed halfspace, and reflection preserves area. Thus its two endpoint contributions sum to at least |A|. Every nonvertical own K cap through zero has area at least 2, by the ordinary simplex centroid inequality. Purely integer caps contain all K and an endpoint. Consequently the depth at (0,0) is at least

    Q=2+81/50=181/50.

The actual caps

    v_i.x-(8/5)z>=0

attain exactly Q: each captures all A because min_A v_i.x=-6/5>-8/5, captures a K simplex cap of area 2, and has zero-area B support trace at v_i.x=8/5. Their middle traces cover the plane, so every middle source has depth at most Q. Endpoint maxima can be isolated and are at most half their own area, namely 81/100 and 36/25, both below Q: the two opposite continuous halfspaces through any point partition the area up to a null line, and one has at most half. Hence Q is the true GLOBAL raw maximum, and r=181/450. The original A cuts are strictly full, not proper; this status is explicitly within the lemma's scope and is not claimed to be an all-proper counterexample.

All three K section coefficients equal 2 and the A sections are zero, so pi_i=1/3. On any edge of K, parameterized from 0 to 1, the middle load is

    W_K=1/3 on [0,1/3) union (2/3,1],
         2/3 on (1/3,2/3).

Boundary points do not affect the integrals. The outer load 1/3 is strictly below r. Nevertheless every unit-height tent has strictly positive cost. To see this, normalize the tent to probability density 2T_t. Its mass in [1/3,2/3] is at least 1/3: for t<=1/3 it is 1/[3(1-t)], for t>=2/3 it is 1/(3t), and for t in the central interval it is 1-1/[9t(1-t)]>=1/2. Thus the mean W_K is at least 4/9, strictly above r by 19/450.

On each edge of length L, (3) therefore satisfies C_K(t)>=(L/2)(19/450)>0. For the two unit-coordinate edges L=3 this lower bound is 19/300; the oblique edge has its actual Euclidean length and the same normalized incidence calculation. This is an exact actual-body obstruction to inferring a pointwise load bound, or descent from one low-load boundary point, from the free middle-tent tests. It is above the OC target and is not an OC counterexample or a claimed local minimizer under all deformations.

The exact verifier `../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_middle_only_face_green_interface_slab_recovery.py` passes 4,143 checks, including actual rational Minkowski vertex inclusion, the three critical caps, oblique reflected-pair cap sums, the tent-potential identity, and the signed-roof formula. The all-halfspace and all-peak statements above follow from their proofs, not from this finite verification.
